glossary.outpouching: A small pocket bulging outward from a hollow organ wall.
glossary.bowel habit: A person's usual pattern of passing stool.
glossary.bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests that rise with inflammation, mainly CRP and white cell count.
glossary.tenderness: Pain when an area is pressed on examination.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the full thickness of the bowel wall.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.palpable mass: A lump that can be felt on examination.
glossary.CT with contrast: CT scan after injecting dye to show blood vessels and inflamed tissue more clearly.
glossary.bowel obstruction: Blockage stopping bowel contents passing through.
glossary.large bowel obstruction: Blockage of the colon or rectum, here from a diverticular stricture.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood tests of kidney function, sodium and potassium.
glossary.Gram-negative: Bacteria with a thin cell wall, such as E. coli, common in the gut.
glossary.anaerobic: Bacteria that live without oxygen, such as Bacteroides in the colon.
glossary.CT-guided: Using CT images to steer a needle or drain into the right place.
glossary.intraluminal pressure: Pressure inside the hollow of the bowel.
glossary.mucosa: Innermost lining layer of the bowel.
glossary.submucosa: Layer of connective tissue and vessels just beneath the mucosa.
glossary.herniation: Pushing of tissue through a weak spot in a wall.
glossary.bacterial overgrowth: Too many bacteria multiplying in one place.
glossary.micro-perforation: A tiny hole in the bowel wall that leaks locally and is often walled off.
glossary.faeculent peritonitis: Peritonitis caused by faeces leaking into the abdominal cavity; very dangerous.
glossary.fibrosis: Scar tissue formation after repeated injury.
glossary.dietary fibre: Plant material that adds bulk to stool and eases its passage.
glossary.IV antibiotics: Antibiotics given directly into a vein.
glossary.acute abdomen: Sudden severe abdominal pain that may need urgent surgery.
glossary.systemically unwell: Ill throughout the body, such as fever, fast pulse or low blood pressure.
glossary.sigmoidoscopy: Camera examination of the rectum and sigmoid colon.
glossary.admission: Being kept in hospital for treatment.
